messages.subject: Repeating transects
parts:
Hello Distance users,

Over the last two years we have been conducting distance surveys
bi-annually to understand our local population of tortoises and this has
yielded some interesting results. There is a bit of discussion on how we
can improve our survey in order to get the most reliable estimates. The
obvious one would be to increase our distances that we cover for our
various habitat types which may be difficult due to terrain. We also
wanted to consider the possibility of repeating transects twice, ether
by having someone follow at a predefined interval, starting at the
opposite side or just repeating the following day. I believe this idea
was briefly mentioned in one of the online videos. After looking though
the distance software (GUI) we are unsure how to prepare our data file
for import and how to tell distance that we have a higher unit of
effort.

If anyone could offer a clue how to do this I would be most appreciative

Regards,
Germano

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Repeating transects
parts:
Germano

For line transects, effort is defined as the amount of travel of the
observers.  Hence, if you have 20 transects, each 1 km in length and
they are all walked twice, the total effort of the survey is 20 * 1 * 2
= 40km and each transect as 2km of effort applied to it.  Short answer:
adjust your line effort to reflect multiple transits.
